context: A working standalone resolver currently exists under private cyberAlchemy-v2 implementation and development paths. It receives normalized intention plus a route catalog and returns selected, ambiguous, or no-route outcomes through a transport-neutral JSON surface, with tests and a browser fixture. Arcanum Bootstrap is the public consumer-install owner and generates native runtime projections for Claude and Codex. The separate cyberalchemy-orchestrator repository is currently classified by accepted Inventory evidence as a workflow-governance control plane, not as the reasoning engine. The research must test one owner-preserving target: a public or consumer-safe resolver capability whose core contract is runtime-neutral; Bootstrap selects or installs it without owning semantic routing; Claude and Codex expose thin native wrappers with behavior parity; the orchestrator may later call it at an input-routing seam without becoming the resolver or reasoning owner; cyberAlchemy-v2 may reference and integrate it at the entry-routing layer while retaining private reasoning-engine authority. The current private package cannot be copied into public Arcanum without an explicit extraction and promotion decision. Entry routing, semantic judgment, actor protocol, effects, and whole-engine readiness must remain distinct.
